candidate.answerReason: The row and column restrictions force A=1 and B=3, giving A+B=4.

methods.label: Use the row and column restrictions
methods.explanation:
The first square of the middle row cannot contain \(1\), because its column already contains \(1\). It cannot contain \(2\), because its row already contains \(2\). Therefore it contains \(3\), leaving \(A=1\).

The top row still needs \(2\) and \(3\). Its middle square cannot contain \(2\), because that column already contains \(2\). Thus the top-right square contains \(2\). The last column now contains \(2\), \(1\), and \(B\), so \(B=3\).

The completed grid is
\[
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline
1&3&2\\\hline
3&2&1\\\hline
2&1&3\\\hline
\end{array}
\]
and satisfies every row and column condition. Hence \(A+B=1+3=4\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
